one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-29 (no 8-K, joint release or denial found through 2026-11-01). In it: (1) the reported Lumentum all-stock deal, which CNBC said could be announced as soon as mid next week (~Nov 4-6) at no big premium; a signing at those terms is largely priced after the -22% two-day fall, and the base rate for big stock-funded acquirers is modest further underperformance (-3.3% vs peers over a year, S&P Global), so we tilt the median ~1% below spot to $194; a collapse of talks would be a sharp positive. (2) NVIDIA's Q3 FY27 report, typically in the second half of November (date not confirmed here), the main read-across for AI capex. (3) Marvell's own Q3 FY27 report is expected around early December (last year 2025-12-02), so it most likely falls just outside the window; its record (8/8 quarters inside the guide, median +0.9% over midpoint) is not a 1-month driver. Short-horizon regularities: reversal after a sharp two-day drop is weak and offset by deal-overhang drift. Spread: lognormal, sigma 0.22 for the month (realized vol 80% / 3.5 = 0.23, trimmed slightly since the realized figure includes the deal spike).

fair_value.method: Quarterly driver build (AI capex x Marvell share of wallet + comms) valued at the horizon on 27.7x NTM P/E (exit rule on the 30.15x 8-peer median, less 1 turn for post-horizon XPU-share and warrant risks) x the build's own adjusted EPS ~$9.55 (w 0.7, $260.63) and a driver-linked normalised-earnings P/E, $7.16 x 25x (w 0.3, $175.12); standalone $237.97, less the Celestial earnout (-$0.80) inside it, and the Lumentum deal at expected value (p 0.59, V -4,639 $M, -2.94 a share). Research target (12m) $234.97.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Normalised-earnings P/E (driver-linked): mid-cycle EPS $7.16 = average FY28-FY29 build revenue $23.25B x 33% x 0.87 / 933M, x 25x through-cycle P/E; less Celestial and deal EV per share

inputs_detail.derivation: eps = (FY28 revenue 19,293 + FY29 27,207) / 2 x 33% x (1 - 13%) / 933M = $7.16, set by driver_build.set from ai_capex, dc_share and comm_rev (supervisor: link it to the drivers). 33% mid-cycle non-GAAP operating margin: Marvell's own last cycle runs from ~26% (Q2 FY25 trough) to ~37% (Q2 FY27), FY25 28.9% and FY26 35.3% (releases): midpoint ~33%. 25x through-cycle P/E: lower half of the 8-peer range (COHR 24.3x, CRDO 25.8x, median 30.15x). Leg value = 25 x 7.16 x (shares pre/post) - Celestial and deal adjustments per share.

methods.name: other

inputs_detail.derivation: P(signed) 0.72: Bloomberg merger rumours 80% accurate within a year and 'advanced stage' wording raises accuracy (Ahern-Sosyura via Quartz), but the same study finds rumours about large, high-profile, highly valued firms significantly less likely to come true (supervisor finding), and MRVL's -13% report-day fall adds walk-away pressure: 0.80 x 0.90 = 0.72. P(not blocked or abandoned by the horizon | signed) 0.82: Stifel says US and China approvals are needed (TheStreet); SAMR cleared 3 of the 5 large semis deals in the cited record (Nvidia/Mellanox after 362 days, so most reviews are still pending at a 12-month horizon, when the market prices the deal at its odds) and failed 2 (Qualcomm/NXP, Intel/Tower); a US-US optical deal has less China overlap. 0.72 x 0.82 = 0.59. We keep 0.59 against the supervisor's 0.56: same evidence, a smaller discount because a pending deal at the horizon is still priced near its terms.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At the supervisor's 0.56 the target is +$0.15; if talks end (p ~0.28) the target is the standalone $237.97.

Optical DSP revenue at FY29 is not disclosed: we take ~$6B (about 40% of FY29 DC revenue ex-custom ~$14.4B, low confidence); a 10% volume loss with p 0.5 = -$0.3B revenue x ~45% incremental margin x (1 - 13%) = -$0.12B a year x 27.7x = -$3.3B; LITE customers that compete with Marvell trimming orders, ~5% of LITE's horizon value x 0.55 = -$3.0B; total ~-$6.5B. Synergies: no figure published; ~$250M pre-tax cost synergies a year x (1 - 13%) x 25x = ~$5.4B, half credited by the horizon = +$2.7B. Costs: banker, legal and retention ~1.1% of the $90B price = -$1.0B.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Supervisor uses +3B / -8B / -1B: -$1.3B more, ~-$0.8/share at p 0.59.

inputs_detail.derivation: Build: V_b = N_H x (combined - standalone) with standalone S = $237.97 (engine, this set without the deal) and N_H = 931.54M: combined = (237.97 x 931.54 + 110,491 + 2,700 - 6,500 - 1,000) / (931.54 + 456.4) = $235.87; V_b = 931.54 x (235.87 - 237.97) = -1,962. Base rate: big stock-funded acquirers underperform peers by ~3.3% over the following year (S&P Global, Russell 3000 2001-2016): V_r = -0.033 x 237.97 x 931.54 = -7,315. Both are low-confidence, so V = average = -4,639; x p 0.59 = -2,737, -$2.94 a share.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Build alone: -$1.24/share expected; base rate alone: -$4.63/share; supervisor -$5.18 (higher standalone value makes each issued share dearer).

upside.story: 90th percentile: AI capex tracks the file's high path (CY27 2,434), the Google and AWS custom programs ramp on time so FY29 revenue approaches ~$38B (toward the Investor Day FY31 path), margins reach ~43.5%, and the P/E holds ~35x; the deal is either struck on better terms or the talks end (worth ~+$3 against this case).

reasoning: Round 2. Base rates first: Marvell's 15 past shocks averaged -31% (GFC -66%, 2022 -58%, 2025 -55%) with a median 5-month recovery (Trefis), so an 80%-vol name warrants a wide, left-skewed 12-month range. Supervisor findings acted on: (1) comms Q3 FY27 guided down low-to-mid teens q/q (Q2 call transcript), so comms is 495/500 in H2 FY27 (round 1 had 570) and DC carries the +20%+ q/q; (2) the normalised leg is now a P/E horizon multiple whose EPS is set by driver_build.set from the drivers; (3) the Celestial earnout liability ($749.5M, 10-Q Note 6) is booked; (4) the Google warrant is priced (share count +0.9%/yr and part of a -1.0 turn); (5) LITE is valued on MarketScreener consensus net income on diluted equity (32.3x today, not the 42.5x blend) and the Stifel DSP dis-synergy is in V; the ad hoc -7% bid-speculation cut is gone. Guidance: 8/8 quarterly revenue guides inside (median +0.9%), GM 7/7 inside at the midpoint, EPS +1.3%: Q3 set at the record-adjusted guide ($3.18B, EPS ~$1.12 vs Street 1.06 and a whisper ~1.07-1.08 = Street + MRVL's usual ~1-2% beat); FY27 EPS ~$4.19 vs Street 4.22 (whisper ~4.25), FY28 ~$7.07 vs Street 7.33 (-3.5%; whisper ~7.40). The FY28 target went ~$16.5B -> ~$18B (August) -> ~$20B (October): a pro-cycle raise pattern, so FY28 sits 3.5% under it and FY29 13% under consensus (capex-file haircut). Margins follow the call's opex rule (opex grows half as fast as revenue) trimmed 1 point. Valuation: 27.7x NTM (exit rule 28.7x less 1 turn for MRVL-specific post-horizon risks) on ~$9.55 (w 0.7) plus normalised $7.16 x 25x (w 0.3): standalone $237.97. Deal p 0.59 (0.72 signed x 0.82 not blocked by the horizon), V = average of the build (-$2.0B) and the stock-acquirer base rate (-3.3%, -$7.3B) = -$4.6B, -$2.94 a share. Research target (12m) $234.97; downside case $93.62; upside case $451.47. We sit below the supervisor's $255.98 mainly on the multiple (27.7x vs 29.0x, from our lower own NTM multiple of 28.4x on Street NTM EPS $6.92 vs its $6.55), the normalised weight (0.3 vs 0.25) and margin (33% vs 34%). Not driver-linked: the deal adjustment (static V). Research limited to ~8 follow-ups; no newer 8-K, release or denial found through 2026-11-01.

downside.story: 10th percentile: AI capex follows the file's low path (CY27 1,390 / CY28 1,265, a 2028 digestion year), Marvell loses share on one hyperscaler XPU generation and the Google ramp slips (dc_share -12%), margins fall 4 points on under-absorbed opex, the P/E de-rates 9 turns (~19x, NVDA/AVGO levels; the normalised leg to 16x), and the Lumentum deal closes at the reported terms (kept at expected value; at signing with DSP-customer backlash the case is a few dollars lower).

upside.story: 90th percentile: AI capex tracks the file's high path (CY27 2,434), the Google and AWS custom programs ramp on time so FY29 revenue approaches ~$38B (toward the Investor Day FY31 path), margins reach ~43.5%, and the P/E holds ~35x; the deal is either struck on better terms or the talks end (worth ~+$3 against this case).

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver set (16 quarters, 6 actual). Value carried by two P/E horizon multiples: 27.7x NTM on the build's own adjusted EPS at the horizon (~$9.55, w 0.7) and a driver-linked normalised-earnings P/E (mid-cycle 33% margin on average FY28-29 revenue, 25x, w 0.3; playbook 0.2-0.4; weights are judgment, untested). Data Center revenue = customer AI capex (standing file, base) x Marvell's share of it; Communications and other is a plain driven segment (100% of revenue is driven). Segment margins are not disclosed: both carry the company non-GAAP operating margin driver. No DCF leg (policy). Adjustments: Celestial earnout (-749.5, p 1) and the Lumentum deal at expected value (p 0.59, static V, not driver-linked). Method-fit flag ('filings too thin') is a tagging artefact: Marvell has a full 10-K/10-Q history; the normalised leg is the non-consensus check.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) deal V rests on our LITE horizon value (18% haircut to consensus): at 12% the build V is ~+$3.5B, at 25% ~-$8.4B; we average the build with the S&P stock-acquirer base rate; (2) -1.0 turn below the exit rule for MRVL-specific post-horizon risks moves the target ~-3.6%; (3) normalised weight 0.3 vs 0.25 moves it ~-1.8%; (4) FY29 revenue 13% under consensus (capex-file haircut). fair_value.value equals the engine base. FY2029 is a 53-week year.

P(signed) 0.72: Bloomberg merger rumours 80% accurate within a year and 'advanced stage' wording raises accuracy (Ahern-Sosyura via Quartz), but the same study finds rumours about large, high-profile, highly valued firms significantly less likely to come true (supervisor finding), and MRVL's -13% report-day fall adds walk-away pressure: 0.80 x 0.90 = 0.72. P(not blocked or abandoned by the horizon | signed) 0.82: Stifel says US and China approvals are needed (TheStreet); SAMR cleared 3 of the 5 large semis deals in the cited record (Nvidia/Mellanox after 362 days, so most reviews are still pending at a 12-month horizon, when the market prices the deal at its odds) and failed 2 (Qualcomm/NXP, Intel/Tower); a US-US optical deal has less China overlap. 0.72 x 0.82 = 0.59. We keep 0.59 against the supervisor's 0.56: same evidence, a smaller discount because a pending deal at the horizon is still priced near its terms.
